Theme

Latin word

sī

conjunction: the indicative for a real condition, the present or perfect subjunctive for a supposed one, the imperfect or pluperfect subjunctive for one contrary to fact

if; if you agree, if you like: the polite way to put a suggestion; if it is no trouble (to you); whether, to see if

In this lexicon

  • if

    the recommended word · classical · Hor. S. 2.6.39: sī vīs, potes; Cato Agr. 1.7: sī mē rogābis, sīc dīcam; Traupman 331

  • suggest

    also used · classical · Cic. Tusc. 1.23: nunc, sī vidētur, hoc, illud aliās; Cic. Q. fr. 3.1.7: sī tibi vidētur

  • trouble

    also used · classical · Cic. Fam. 13.73.2: velim, sī tibi grave nōn erit, mē certiōrem faciās (Lewis & Short s.v. gravis); Traupman 110, 398

  • whether

    also used · classical · Petr. 33.2: temptēmus tamen, sī adhūc sorbilia sunt; Phaedr. 4.8.3–4: haec cum temptāret sī qua rēs esset cibī

  • sī ita est: case

    classical

  • sī modo: condition

    classical

  • sī Dominus voluerit: God willing

    late Latin

  • quod sī (quodsī): if

    classical

  • sī nōn: if not

    classical

  • sī minus: if not

    classical

  • sī tibi vidētur: mind

    classical

  • quid sī …?: suppose

    classical

  • Ō sī tacuissēs, philosophus mānsissēs.: you put your foot in your mouth
